solution:
Group the factors using the difference of two squares:
$$(1-2x)^5(1+2x)^5=\bigl((1-2x)(1+2x)\bigr)^5=(1-4x^2)^5.$$

Then the whole expression is
$$(1-4x^2)^5(1+4x^2)^5=\bigl((1-4x^2)(1+4x^2)\bigr)^5=(1-16x^4)^5.$$

Expanding $(1-16x^4)^5$ by the binomial theorem, the term in $x^{12}=(x^4)^3$ is
$$\binom{5}{3}(-16x^4)^3=10\cdot(-16)^3x^{12}=-10\cdot4096\,x^{12}=-2^{13}\cdot5\,x^{12},$$
since $10\cdot4096=40960$ and $2^{13}\cdot5=8192\cdot5=40960$.

So the coefficient of $x^{12}$ is $-2^{13}\times5$.

The answer is **A**.
